chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three things are the pride and adornment of the Believer in this world and the Hereafter: Prayer at the end of the night, his dejection from what is in the hands of people, and his Wilayah (guardianship) of the Imam from the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them).'

He said: 'And three are the worst of the creatures, by whom the best of the creatures were tested: Abu Sufyan, one of them, who fought the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and was inimical to him; and Muawiya, who fought Ali (peace be upon him) and was inimical to him; and Yazeed ibn Muawiya, may Allah curse him, who fought Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and was inimical to him until he killed him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three virtues of a believer and the three worst creatures in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi delineates the spiritual pillars of a believer—night prayer, contentment, and Imamate—while contrasting them with the 'worst of creatures' who tested the elite through their enmity. It specifically links Abu Sufyan, Muawiya, and Yazeed to the trials faced by the Prophet, Ali, and Al-Husayn respectively, emphasizing the historical continuity of leadership and opposition within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition. The mention of 'testing the best of creation' underscores the theological significance of these figures in Shia historiography as key agents of fitna.

en.hubeali: H 14759 – Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying; ‘Three things are a matter of pride for the Believer and an adornment of him in the world and the Hereafter – The Prayer during the last part of the night, and his dejection from what is in the hands of the people, and his Wilayah of the Imamasws from the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww.

And the three who are the most evil of the creatures by whom the people were plagued, are Abu Sufyan who fought against the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> during his era and was inimical to him<sup>saww</sup>, and Muawiya fought against Ali<sup>asws</sup> and was inimical to him<sup>asws</sup>, and Yazeed Bin Muawiya, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him<sup>la</sup>, fought against Al-Husayn Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and was inimical to him<sup>asws</sup> until he<sup>la</sup> killed him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 311. Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying; ‘Three things are a matter of pride for the Believer and an adornment of him in the world and the Hereafter – The Prayer during the last part of the night, and his dejection from what is in the hands of the people, and his Wilayah of the Imam (a.s.) from the Progeny (a.s.) of Muhammad (saww).

And the three who are the most evil of the creatures by whom the people were plagued, are Abu Sufyan who fought against the Rasool Allah (saww) during his era and was inimical to him (saww), and Muawiya fought against Ali (a.s.) and was inimical to him (a.s.), and Yazeed Bin Muawiya, may Allah (azwj) Curse him (la), fought against Al-Husayn Bin Ali (a.s.), and was inimical to him (a.s.) until he (la) killed him (a.s.)’.
